title: WASM runner spike (Pyodide load size/perf, lazy-load, cache, offline fallback)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). Pyodide's WASM bundle is large and could severely degrade the beginner experience on slow connections. If lazy-load and caching strategies are not proven viable in a spike before the full runner is built, the in-browser runner (occ-runner-104) may need a redesign.
objective: Spike the Pyodide WASM runner to measure load size and performance characteristics, evaluate lazy-load and caching strategies, identify the graceful offline/no-WASM fallback approach, and record a decision on whether Pyodide is viable for the in-browser runner.
acceptanceCriteria: Pyodide bundle load size is measured on a simulated slow connection (≤ 4 Mbps); results are recorded.
Lazy-load and service-worker caching strategies are prototyped and their impact on first-load vs. repeat-load time is measured.
A graceful fallback ('download to run locally') is designed for environments where WASM is unavailable.
Spike concludes with a written recommendation: proceed with Pyodide (with noted load mitigations) or pivot to an alternative.
Results and recommendation are reviewed by the Maintainer before proceeding to occ-runner-104.
output: A spike report committed to the repository documenting Pyodide load measurements, lazy-load/cache findings, offline fallback design, and a go/no-go recommendation for the in-browser runner.
